## Exercise 7.1: A sentinel for the index {#ex-7.1}

```python
rule bowtie2_index:
    input:
        fasta = data_path(config["reference"]["fasta"]),
    output:
        done = touch(OUT + "/reference/bowtie2_index.done"),          # <1>
    log:
        LOGS + "/bowtie2_index/bowtie2_index.log",
    benchmark:
        BENCH + "/bowtie2_index/bowtie2_index.tsv",
    threads: 4
    conda: ENVS + "/regpipe_align.yml"
    params:
        prefix = OUT + "/reference/bowtie2_index/genome",
    shell:
        """
        mkdir -p $(dirname {params.prefix})                            # <2>
        bowtie2-build --threads {threads} {input.fasta} {params.prefix} > {log} 2>&1
        """
```
1. `touch()` makes Snakemake create the marker itself after the command
   succeeds, so the shell command does not need a `touch {output}` line.
   ChromSimPipe writes `touch {output.done}` by hand instead; the effect is
   the same.
2. Our first try left this out and failed: `bowtie2-build` does not create
   the folder for its prefix, and Snakemake only creates the folders of
   *declared* outputs. It made `output/reference/` for the marker, not
   `output/reference/bowtie2_index/`.

`align` needs no change. Its input is `rules.bowtie2_index.output`, which is
now the marker, and its `params.index` is still the prefix `INDEX_PREFIX`. The
dry run still lists 61 jobs, and the filtered BAM for `HCT116_CTCF_1` has the
same 24,434 reads as with `directory()`.

Then we deleted `output/reference/bowtie2_index/genome.1.bt2` and ran the dry
run again:

```
Nothing to be done (all requested files are present and up to date).
```

The marker is there, so Snakemake is satisfied, and the next new `align` job
would fail inside bowtie2. That is the price of a sentinel. `directory()`
behaves the same way here; only `multiext()`, which names each file, notices.

## Exercise 7.2: Count the jobs {#ex-7.2}

Scatter replaces each of the 10 `align` jobs with one `split_fastq`, N
`align_chunk` and one `merge_chunks`:

```
jobs = 61 - 10 + 10 + 10 * N + 10 = 71 + 10 * N
```

| `scatter_chunks` | jobs |
|---:|---:|
| 0 (off) | 61 |
| 1 | 81 |
| 3 | 101 |
| 4 | 111 |

We checked 1, 3 and 4 with dry runs, and `tests/test_dryrun.py` checks 3
(module 8).

`scatter_chunks: 1` is not useful for speed: it adds a split and a merge around
one alignment, 20 extra jobs that do nothing. It is useful as a test. It runs
the scatter code path with the smallest number of jobs, so if you change
`split_fastq.py` or the merge you can check the result is the same as with
scatter off.

## Exercise 7.3: Why did align rerun? {#ex-7.3}

The aligned BAM is `temp()`:

```python
    output:
        bam = temp(OUT + "/{sample}/{sample}_aligned.bam"),    # <1>
```
1. Snakemake deleted this file as soon as `filter`, the only job that reads it,
   had finished.

When `minMapq` changes, `filter` has to run again, and its input no longer
exists. The only way to get it back is to run `align` again. The dry run says so:
`align` has `reason: Missing output files`.

To rerun only `filter`, keep the aligned BAMs: remove `temp()` from the
`align` output (and from `merge_chunks`, which writes the same file when
scatter is on). We tried it on a fresh output folder: after the change, the
same `minMapq=20` dry run lists one job, `filter`.

The cost is disk space. You keep a second BAM per sample: 1.5 MB for
`HCT116_CTCF_1` on the course data, far more on a whole-genome library. The
lab default is `temp()`, because a MAPQ change is rare and an alignment is
cheap compared with keeping every intermediate file. If you are about to tune
the filter, remove `temp()` for a while, or run with `--notemp`, which keeps
`temp()` files for that run.

## Exercise 7.4: Make ChromSimPipe notice {#ex-7.4}

Two ways, with different costs.

The first is to make the config file an input:

```python
rule simulateShard:
    input:
        validated = f"{L('done')}/validateCTCF.done",
        config    = CONFIGFILE,                         # <1>
        ...
```
1. Now the `mtime` trigger sees the file. Any edit to it reruns every shard of
   every condition and locus.

This is one line and it is never wrong, but it is blunt. Fixing a comment, or
changing an analysis setting that the simulation never reads, reruns every
GPU job.

The second is to pass the values the rule uses as params:

```python
    params:
        configfile = CONFIGFILE,
        condition_settings = lambda wildcards: str(COND_LOOKUP[wildcards.condition]),   # <1>
```
1. The settings of this job's condition, as text. The `params` trigger compares
   it with the stored value, so only conditions whose settings changed rerun.
   `COND_LOOKUP` is ChromSimPipe's per-condition dictionary; the scripts would
   still read the file, this param only tells Snakemake what to watch.

This reruns exactly what changed, but only for the values you listed. A
parameter the script reads that is not in the param is invisible again, so
someone has to keep the list in step with `configs/parameters.py`.

A third option is the one the repository documents today: delete the `.done`
markers of the steps you want to redo. It costs nothing to set up and relies
on you remembering. For a pipeline where one rerun is hours of GPU time,
params for the simulation settings are probably worth the upkeep, and the
config file as an input is fine for the cheap analysis steps.
